method:
ONE PROCEDURE. A scribe writes a whole book, page by page, carrying three things and nothing else: a letter jig, a word tray, and a quire packet. No meaning, no morphology, no phrase, no word list outside his own working stock.

THE LETTER JIG. An order-2 chain over strokes. Its alphabet is the strokes of the manuscript's own transcription (EVA-basic, 31 of them) plus three marks: a word end; a line end, which is written as one mark, so that a word ending a line ends with the line; and the paragraph mark that stands before an opening line. Every place is looked up in eight tables at once and they are blended -- the two strokes before, in this setting (an ordinary line, or the opening line of a paragraph, which he sets up before writing), at a line end or not, in this part of the book in this hand; then the same with the hand dropped, then the part of the book, then the line-end setting, then one stroke of history. Each table takes the weight n/(n+8) where n is how often it has seen the place, and what the closer tables leave is left to the whole-book table, so no probability is lost. The jig holds the pen: at every stroke it is asked whether the word ends here, and on a line end only the line-end mark may close it.

THE WORD TRAY. Before the jig writes a word he may take a slip he has already written. Sixteen times in a hundred he lifts one from the tray of the last ten words, the nearer ones lying on top (a geometric reach, tau 3 words), and alters one stroke in it: the stroke is drawn from the jig at that place, must fit the stroke that follows it in the word, and may not be the stroke standing there already. Sixteen times in a hundred he takes a whole slip from the pile of the page, and twelve times in a hundred one from the packet. A slip is lifted with a weight for how the jig would take it up -- the fitted probability of its first stroke in this place -- because he lifts the word his pen is already set for.

THE QUIRE PACKET. Every 12 pages he stocks a packet of 420 slips from the working stock of the part of the book he is in, in the hand that writes it, and does not restock it mid-quire. A page's stock is 35 per cent drawn from the packet and the rest afresh from the same working stock.

THE LINE IS WRITTEN TO THE MARGIN. He draws the width of the line from the fitted distribution of line widths -- strokes, with one space between words, mean 45.4 on the public pages -- lays word after word while the next one fits, and where the room left is too small for the word he has just written he tries up to three more forms and takes one that fits if one comes; if none does, the line ends where it stands. A form he rejects is not written and does not enter his tray. The word that stands at the line's end gets the closing stroke of his line-end habit: the jig, at that place with the line-end setting on, is asked which stroke closes a word there, and the last stroke is drawn again from that answer.

FITTED ON PUBLIC PAGES ONLY. Every table, rate and distribution above is fitted on the 192 training pages of the public practice split, the complement of the 34 pages the practice evaluation scores; those 34 are never read. The book's layout -- page order, which lines open a paragraph, which part of the book each page belongs to, which hand writes it -- is the codicological record rather than the text, and the scorer lays the lines onto it page by page as a scribe's lines go onto a quire. The text itself is meaningless and knows nothing of the pages it is laid on.

WHAT IT DOES TO F-023. On the held-out practice pages the share of certain words of at most three units is 0.4403 at line ends against 0.3440 on the same lines away from the ends: ratio 1.2681, against the manuscript's own 0.3701 against 0.3079, ratio 1.1575. It beats the within-line shuffle null at p = 0.0025 on 399 permutations, which is the floor of the test. Nothing in the procedure mentions word length, or line ends, or a ratio between them. The shortness of line-endings falls out of filling a ruled line to the margin: when the room left is small, the forms that fit are the short ones.

CONTROLS, same generator, same fit, measured on public 40-page samples (ratio of the at-most-three share at line ends to mid-line; the manuscript's own value on the public training pages is 1.115). Margin-filling with three shorter forms tried: 1.24. With one form tried: 1.13. With none -- the line simply stops when the next word will not fit: 0.98, the fact is gone. So it is the ruled margin, not the line-end habit and not the letter jig, that carries F-023. The number of attempts, 3, was set on the public training pages by that comparison before the held-out pages were read; the band, the null and the held-out pages were used to choose nothing.

IT IS NOT A LUCKY SEED. Seeds 11, 12, 13, 14 give 1.2681, 1.2533, 1.3192, 1.2916 on the held-out practice pages, every one passing at p = 0.0025.

A FINDING ABOUT THE FACT ITSELF, from the public pages only. On 20 random 34-page subsets of the 192 public training pages, the manuscript's OWN value of this ratio ranges 0.935 to 1.289 (median 1.120) and falls below the fact's threshold of 1 on 1 subset of 20. The threshold is inside the sampling noise of the quantity it states: a draw of 34 pages of the manuscript itself can fail the first half of F-023. This text is above 1 on 20 of 20 such subsets (1.214 to 1.398, median 1.331), so its pass is not the same kind of pass the manuscript's own value would be on an unlucky draw.

WHAT ELSE THE SAME TEXT REPRODUCES. It was not aimed at any other fact, and on the same held-out practice pages it reproduces 15 of the 21 established ones: F-002, F-003, F-004, F-005, F-007, F-008, F-009, F-013, F-016, F-017, F-018, F-019, F-021, F-022, F-023. It does not reproduce F-001 (line-final m in Currier B), F-006 (line-opening words longer than within-line shuffle), F-010 (edge dependence breaking at line ends), F-011 (nearby pages sharing words), F-014 (two types in three occurring once) or F-020 (pages of one Currier language sharing words).

GUARDS. 4,487 ordinary lines and 738 paragraph-opening lines, exactly the manuscript's own counts, so the text fills every page of the book; 43,870 tokens, 8,663 distinct, mean length 4.38 units; 0 four-word runs of the manuscript; 0 uncertainty markers.

WHAT IT WOULD SHOW, if it holds on the hidden pages: that a text with no language in it, written by a hand that only knows how strokes follow strokes, what his pen is set for, and where the margin is, can carry the elevation of short words at line ends. The fact would then be a statement about ruled pages and justification, not about meaning or about the shape of a vocabulary. WHAT IT WOULD NOT SHOW: that the manuscript was written by such a scribe -- only that this fact cannot tell the two apart. ASSUMPTION THAT COULD FAIL ON THE HIDDEN PAGES: the hidden pages are one draw of 34, and on public draws of that size this text's ratio ranges 1.21 to 1.40 and the null's floor is p = 0.0025, so a failure would mean the hidden pages are unlike any public draw; the section and hand mix of the hidden pages also enters, since the jig and the stock are kept per part of the book and per hand.
